documents.title: Derive a candidate from the controlling predicates
documents.content: For each uncovered assignment, first walk backward through its enclosing if/case predicates and data dependencies. Write the necessary path condition before choosing operands. If two necessary predicates contradict each other, emit a proof obligation instead of a speculative stimulus. A satisfiable fixed-input witness establishes legality, not execution of the internal line.

documents.title: FP normalization and rounding-carry candidate
documents.content: For a rounding branch, target its guard/sticky predicate and the carry out of the rounded fraction, not merely a large result. A prior ALU run used (FP_ADD, 0x3fffffff, 0x40000000) for the round-carry cluster. Treat that tuple as a project-local example: reuse it only when the current backward slice contains the same normalization and rounding predicates.

documents.title: FP cancellation into the underflow path
documents.content: For subtraction underflow, choose close small normal operands so cancellation forces a left normalization beyond the available exponent. The prior ALU run used (FP_SUB, 0x00800001, 0x00800000). This is a pattern for the s4_shift_amt/s4_new_exp/UNDERFLOW cluster, not a generic answer for every zero-result line.

documents.title: Check FP2INT interval arithmetic before proposing input
documents.content: Translate nested FP2INT branches into one interval before selecting bits. In this ALU, the normal-conversion arm requires 127 <= f2i_exp < 158, while f2i_shift_right = 158 - f2i_exp. Therefore the nested condition f2i_shift_right >= 32 cannot hold in that arm; record it for a reachability proof. Do not repeat the 0.5 input: it takes the earlier f2i_exp < 127 branch.

documents.title: FP2INT special values select their own early branches
documents.content: Target FP2INT NaN/invalid through the special-value predicate, before normal conversion. A prior ALU run used (FP2INT, 0x7fc00000, 0x00000000) to enter f2i_is_nan and set fp2int_invalid. Keep this separate from finite values below 1, which take the f2i_exp < 127 zero-result branch.

documents.title: A case default may be structurally unreachable
documents.content: Do not target a sequential case default through an unrelated opcode. Check the state transition invariant. In this ALU, while fp_active is true fp_counter visits 1, 2, 3, and 4; state 4 clears fp_active. The default arm is therefore a proof obligation, not an AND/NOT stimulus candidate.

documents.title: Distinguish opcode decode branches from internal FP branches
documents.content: For an output-mux default guarded by int_done_r, use a reserved opcode (0xA..0xF) and force an input change so the done pipeline fires. This can cover the reserved-op output branch, but it cannot cover defaults inside the fp_active or fp2int_active state machines. Keep those obligations separate.

documents.title: Write one typed Scala tuple per independent intent
documents.content: Use a short unique snake_case label and a tuple (label, opcode, a, b). Spell each 32-bit bit-pattern as a non-negative hexadecimal Long literal with the L suffix, including zero as 0x00000000L. Group lines governed by the same predicate into one intent; do not create one redundant tuple per assignment line.

documents.title: Separate candidate, witness, replay, and proof
documents.content: Use four distinct claims: the model proposes a candidate; JasperGold finds a legal witness; VCS/URG replay establishes coverage closure; a dedicated reachability property establishes dead code. Never report a solved fixed-input cover as evidence that a particular internal RTL line executed.
